title.narrative: OC 2.2 Number of new Sexual Assault & Referral Centres (SARCs), shelters, justice and social support service mechanisms put in place and delivering services with the support of the programme per year and per focal state

description.narrative: This is a twopart quantitative indicator that counts the total number of justice and social support service mechanisms that have been put in place by the RoLACII Programme and are able to deliver services as a result of the support provided by the RoLACII Programme. In the context of the RoLACII Programme, justice and social support service mechanisms include but are not limited to Sexual Assault Referral Centres (SARCs), shelters and safe spaces established by government, private sector or civil society, Sexual and Genderbased Violence (SGBV) Response teams established by government or civil society, Sexual and Genderbased Violence (SGBV) Courts, Sexual Offender Databases, Police Gender Desks, Police Family Support Units, Disability Help Desks, Disability Commissions established by government, Family Courts, Schoolbased response and referral mechanisms, Communitybased Child Protection Committees; and any other justice or social support mechanism that supports access to rights and justice for women, children and persons with disabilities in Nigeria. Disability Desks Service: desk within an MDA or justice service provider established to address and support the need of PWDS

title.narrative: OC 1.3 Number of persons benefitting from diversion and noncustodial measures each year in focal states of the programme (disaggregated by sex and age)

description.narrative: This is a twopart quantitative indicator that counts 1. The number of criminal complaints that are diverted from the criminal justice system (formal arraignment in courts) and 2. The number of offenders who are sentenced to one noncustodial measure or the other and complete the sentence.Diversion, any of a variety of programs that implement strategies seeking to avoid the formal processing of an offender by the criminal justice system. A typical diversion program results in a person who has been accused of a crime being directed into a treatment or care program as an alternative to criminal prosecution and punishment. NonCustodial measures: A noncustodial measure is an alternative sentence that avoids imprisonment. Under the Nigerian Correctional Service Act, a noncustodial measure includes community service, probation, parole, restorative justice measures and other noncustodial measures that a court may assign. Under the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015, noncustodial measures include fines, suspended sentences, restitution and compensation
Outcomes

description.narrative: This is a quantitative indicator that counts the number of substantive criminal justice, anticorruption and access to justice interventions replicated in nonfocal states from those implemented by RoLAC in its focal states. These counts will be per specific intervention in a state that is not one of RoLACII focal/ target states.An intervention will be considered to be substantive if stakeholders are actively engaged in designing and delivering the intervention. Stakeholders will be expected to show a willingness to continue implementing an intervention post RoLACs support.

title.narrative: Ibrahim Index of African Governance (Accountability and Transparency)

description.narrative: This indicator reports the ranking assigned to Nigeria in the Ibrahim Index (IIAG) Governance Indicators for its performance in the area of the Control of Corruption. The IIAG is a tool that measures and monitors governance performance in African countries. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation (MIF) defines governance as the provision of political, social, economic and environmental public goods and services that every citizen has the right to expect from their government, and that a government has the responsibility to deliver to its citizens. In the IIAG, country performance in delivering governance is measured across four key components (Safety & Rule of Law, Participation & Human Rights), that effectively provides indicators of a countries Overall Governance performance.

This indicator reports the score assigned to Nigeria in the Global State of Democracy Index. Launched in November 2017, by International IDEA, the Global State of Democracy (GSoD) report provides annual evidencebased analysis and data on the global and regional state of democracy across 174 countries globally. The GSoD conceptual framework is based on five attributes of democracy: 1. Representative Government; 2. Fundamental Rights, 3. Checks on Government, 5. Impartial Administration and Participatory Engagement. The access to justice sub attribute under Fundamental human rights denotes the extent to which the legal system is fair (i.e., citizens are not subject to arbitrary arrest or detention and have the right to be under the jurisdiction of, and to seek redress from, competent, independent and impartial tribunals without undue delay). Scoring runs from 0 to 1, with 0 representing the lowest achievement in the whole sample and 1 the highest.

This indicator reports the ranking/score assigned to Nigeria in the annual World Justice Project Governance Indicators (WJP) for its performance in the area of the Rule of Law. Each year the World Justice Project which is an independent Project Founded by William H. Neukom in 2006, collates information from a wide range of sources about the standing of the rule of law in most countries in the world. Each country is assigned a ranking which reflects its position in the overall table in a fiverank system (where 0.00 is the weakest and 1.00 is the strongest score).It is noted that this indicator reflects Nigerias overall ranking. However, the contribution/s of RoLACII may be small, given the number of beneficiary states as well as other factors.
